title: dedicated-autoscaler-priority-routing-burst-util-reporting-enhancement-v43
author: Samira Patel
description:
Motivation: Improve Dedicated autoscaler behavior for mixed-priority fleets to (1) respect per-priority throughput guarantees, (2) smooth token-bucket bursts to avoid short-lived capacity spikes, and (3) provide richer utilization reporting for SRE and product analytics. This PR implements priority-aware routing at the autoscaler level, adds a burst_capacity config and smoothing window, and exports new Prometheus metrics for per-priority utilization and tail queue statistics. Changes include: feature toggles for gradual rollout, migration docs for admin operators, unit and integration tests, and a canary deployment plan.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement priority routing and weighting
- [x] Add burst token-bucket smoothing with configurable window
- [x] Emit per-priority utilization metrics (p50/p90/p95/p99, queue_length, burst_consumption)
- [x] Add config + API changes to FleetSpec with validation
- [x] Update Helm chart defaults and values schema
- [x] Add migration guide and operator notes
- [x] Integration tests and perf bench results attached

Implementation notes:
- Autoscaler: added priority_weights and throughput_guarantee_pct fields; routing algorithm now factors guaranteed throughput first, then best-effort capacity. When guaranteed capacity cannot be satisfied immediately, the scheduler enqueues requests with priority metadata instead of immediately triggering scale-up; this reduces churn and enables smarter batching.
- Burst smoothing: replaced the previous instantaneous tokenbucket increment with a sliding-window refill implementation (default window 30s) to bound short-term ingestion spikes. Smoothing window and max_burst_capacity are configurable per-fleet and per-priority.
- Metrics: new metrics exported under redwood_dedicated_fleet_utilization_* with labels {fleet, priority}. Added both rate and histogram metrics for queueing and burst_consumption to make regressions visible in Console dashboards.
- Backwards compatibility: all new FleetSpec fields are optional and default to previous behavior; a feature flag `enable_new_autoscaler_v2` controls rollout.
- Testing & perf: microbench against a mixed-priority trace shows 18% reduction in peak instance churn and 12% lower 95th latency for guaranteed requests after smoothing. Canary rollout performed over 3 steps with automated rollback on error budget regressions.
